facts.text: Secondary hazards of an automatic stop are new dangers created by the stop itself: being struck from behind, blocking an escape route, stalling or rolling back on a grade, spilling the load, or hurting the operator.
facts.quote: Secondary hazards are the new dangers an automatic stop creates by itself: being struck from behind, blocking an escape route, stalling or rolling back on a grade, spilling the load, or hurting the operator.

facts.text: A machine that halts without warning in a line of haul trucks can be hit by the truck behind.
facts.quote: A machine that halts without warning in a line of haul trucks can be hit by the one behind

facts.text: US insurance data showed that forward collision warning with automatic braking raised the rate of being struck from behind by 20 percent; the booklet cites this on-road result as a caution about automatic stopping.
facts.quote: in US insurance data, forward collision warning with automatic braking raised the rate of being struck from behind by 20 percent, a road result the booklet quotes as a caution [Chapter 4].

facts.text: A machine stopped in a narrow underground roadway can block the escape route of the workers the machine was protecting.
facts.quote: A machine that stops in a narrow underground roadway can block the escape route of the workers it was protecting

facts.text: Workers reported walking backwards into the tailgate of stopped haulage.
facts.quote: workers reported "walking backwards into the tailgate" of stopped haulage [Chapter 4].

facts.text: A machine stopped on a ramp may be unable to restart smoothly and can roll back or roll forward when the automatic brake releases.
facts.quote: A machine stopped on a ramp may be unable to restart smoothly, and when the automatic brake releases it can roll back or roll forward

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 warns that discontinuing an intervention must not create rollaway.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-3 warns that discontinuing an intervention must not create rollaway

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 recommends an operator action, such as applying the parking brake, before releasing an automatic braking intervention.
facts.quote: recommends an operator action, such as applying the parking brake, before release [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Hard braking can spill rock, swing a suspended load or tip a high-loaded machine; sudden stops can jar the operator.
facts.quote: Hard braking can spill rock, swing a suspended load or tip a high-loaded machine, and sudden stops jar the operator

facts.text: MSHA engineers estimate that seat belts could save three to four miners' lives per year, supporting the importance of restraints during an automatic stop.
facts.quote: MSHA engineers estimate that three to four miners' lives a year could be saved by seat belts, one reason restraint matters for an automatic stop [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The booklet identifies immobilization in an unsafe location, loss of traction or control, operator counteraction, production loss, and eventual operator disabling of a system that stops too often as additional hazards of automatic stopping.
facts.quote: The booklet also names immobilization in an unsafe location, loss of traction or control, operator counteraction, production loss, and the long-run hazard that operators disable a system that stops them too often [Chapters 1, 4, 8].

facts.text: The booklet reports that secondary hazards of automatic stopping have not been measured off-road; mining sources contained no findings of spilled loads, slope instability or rear-end strikes caused by automatic braking.
facts.quote: Off-road, none of these has been measured: spilled loads, slope instability and rear-end strikes caused by automatic braking were not found in the mining sources

facts.text: No injury or jerk threshold exists for haul trucks, loaders or dozers in the booklet's discussion of automatic-stop secondary hazards.
facts.quote: no injury or jerk threshold exists for haul trucks, loaders or dozers [Chapter 4].

facts.text: The automatic-braking safety goal cannot be limited to stopping before the object; the transition from warning to intervention needs its own hazard analysis.
facts.quote: The safety goal cannot be "stop before the object". The transition from warning to intervention needs its own hazard analysis

facts.text: The automatic-braking simulation matrix needs hazardous-unintended-intervention cases as well as failure-to-intervene cases.
facts.quote: the simulation matrix needs hazardous-unintended-intervention cases as well as failure-to-intervene cases [Chapters 1, 10].

facts.text: The physical test campaign should include hold-and-restart tests on grade and stability tests to address secondary hazards of automatic stopping.
facts.quote: Hold-and-restart tests on grade and stability tests belong in the physical campaign for this reason [Chapter 8].
